Subject: Stellate renewal conversation — capacity uplift & performance proof

Hi Lauren,

Quick note from our side as we start renewal talks: were seeing increasing latency and token cost from our current provider and were evaluating options. Wed like to understand whether Redwood can commit to a 2x capacity uplift over our current committed throughput and provide a short performance proof (single-day load run and latency breakdown) prior to signing an extended term. Also procurement will need a tiered price schedule if we escalate usage.

Key asks:
- Can you run a 1-day canary load test that shows 95th pct latency at our P95 SLA for a 60M tokens/day pattern?
- Updated tiered pricing for 2x and 3x committed throughput (12/24 month term options).
- Evidence of isolation plan (dedicated pool) and fallback for spot shortages.

Our renewal window is tight — we need the proof and pricing by Nov 18 to get internal approvals. Im happy to hop on a quick call to align scope.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of AI Platform | Stellate Commerce

1) Redwood will run a targeted canary on a Dedicated pool that mirrors your traffic shape (well use the requirements you attached). Estimated test window: 6 hours for steady-state then ramp for 2 hours.
2) Deliverables: latency report (P50/P95/P99), cost-per-token delta, and a short ops runbook for burst scaling.
3) Pricing: Ill share an initial tiered term sheet (12/24) for 2x/3x throughput; Marissa will size Dedicated capacity and propose commit levels.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm availability for an operational kickoff today or tomorrow? We need the canary executed and the report back to Alex by Nov 17 to leave a business day for procurement review.

Looping in ops and benchmarks. We can run the requested validation — proposed plan below and I attached the detailed throughput report template we will populate.

Validation plan (high level):
- Environment: Dedicated pool (pinned GPUs, isolation) matching Stellates current inference profile.
- Test profile: 60M token/day steady baseline; 2x/3x spike windows to show scaling behavior.
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency per model variant, token cost, GPU utilization, error rates.
- Runbook: Warm KV cache for 1 hour before steady run, then 6-hour steady-state, then two controlled ramp-ups.

Preliminary capacity proposal:
- Tier A (2x commit): reserved 8-slot pool — monthly commit X, 12-month discount Y%.
- Tier B (3x commit): reserved 12-slot pool + burst credits — monthly commit X2, 24-month discount Y2%.

Ill attach the throughput_report_q2.xlsx after the first run. Need Ops signoff (Rishi) and model engineer availability (Karthik) to schedule the canary for Nov 16. If the canary passes we can convert the test environment config into a short-term contract attachment for procurement to review.

Attachments: throughput_report_q2.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_proof_plan_v2.pdf (pdf)

Update for internal owners and Stellate: canary run completed this morning and results are attached. High-level summary:

- Canary outcome: Dedicated pool met P95 SLA for the 2x steady-state profile; P99 shows expected tail under sustained 3x bursts but within our documented degradation envelope.
- Cost delta: estimated +18% per-token for Dedicated reserved pool vs. their current provider at baseline, tier discounts applied for 12/24 month commits reduce incremental cost to +8% (12m) and +2% (24m) for the 3x scenario.
- Ops notes: warm KV cache policy and pre-warm window recommended prior to shift; we can automate pre-warm as part of the migration plan.

Deliverables attached: throughput_report_q2.xlsx, redwood_proof_plan_v2.pdf. Ive also uploaded a draft DocuSign term doc to the linked HubSpot/DocuSign URL for procurement to review.

Action items:
- Marissa: convert canary config into a 30-day trial attachment and pass to Procurement for signature (non-binding).
- Karthik: prepare an ops checklist to support a phased cutover (include rollback gating).
- Rishi: confirm SLA language for Dedicated and provide an emergency escalation path.

Alex / Procurement: please confirm if the draft doc addresses procurements needs or if you want specific language edits. If procurement is happy, we can trigger the DocuSign flow and lock in the 24-month commit discount before EOD Friday.

Thanks everyone — good collaborative work on a tight timeline.
